--------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m8p2t5 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Locations

VARIABLES stock, level, fineLoc, override
\* stock: blood units held at each storage location; level: bank lock level
\* (idle/coarse/fine); fineLoc: the fine-locked source location; override:
\* whether the admin override is engaged.

vars == <<stock, level, fineLoc, override>>

Total == 3
None == "none"

RECURSIVE SumStock(_)
SumStock(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET l == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN stock[l] + SumStock(S \ {l})

TypeOK ==
    /\ stock \in [Locations -> 0..Total]
    /\ level \in {"idle", "coarse", "fine"}
    /\ fineLoc \in Locations \cup {None}
    /\ override \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ stock = [l \in Locations |-> IF l = "fridge" THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ level = "idle"
    /\ fineLoc = None
    /\ override = FALSE

\* Take the coarse bank-wide lock.
LockCoarse ==
    /\ level = "idle"
    /\ level' = "coarse"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, fineLoc, override>>

\* Take a fine lock on a specific source location.
LockFine(l) ==
    /\ level = "coarse"
    /\ fineLoc = None
    /\ fineLoc' = l
    /\ level' = "fine"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, override>>

\* Move one unit from the fine-locked source to another location.
Transfer(dst) ==
    /\ level = "fine"
    /\ fineLoc # None
    /\ dst # fineLoc
    /\ stock[fineLoc] > 0
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![fineLoc] = @ - 1, ![dst] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<level, fineLoc, override>>

\* Drop the fine lock.
UnlockFine ==
    /\ level = "fine"
    /\ level' = "coarse"
    /\ fineLoc' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, override>>

\* Drop the coarse lock.
UnlockCoarse ==
    /\ level = "coarse"
    /\ level' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, fineLoc, override>>

\* Under admin override, move a unit directly, bypassing the lock stack.
AdminTransfer(src, dst) ==
    /\ override
    /\ src # dst
    /\ stock[src] > 0
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![src] = @ - 1, ![dst] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<level, fineLoc, override>>

\* Toggle the admin override.
ToggleOverride ==
    /\ override' = ~override
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, level, fineLoc>>

Next ==
    \/ LockCoarse
    \/ \E l \in Locations : LockFine(l)
    \/ \E dst \in Locations : Transfer(dst)
    \/ UnlockFine
    \/ UnlockCoarse
    \/ \E src, dst \in Locations : AdminTransfer(src, dst)
    \/ ToggleOverride

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every transfer only relocates a unit between locations, so the bank's total
\* blood-unit count is invariant.
Conserved == SumStock(Locations) = Total
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Locations = {"fridge", "counter", "lab"}
INVARIANT Conserved
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker moves blood units among several storage locations -- the fridge, the issue counter, and the lab. Because a misplaced unit is dangerous, unit moves are serialized with hierarchical locks: the bank takes a coarse bank-wide lock first, then a fine lock on a specific source location, before it may move a unit out of that source. Moving a unit takes one unit from the fine-locked source and adds it to a destination location; units are only ever relocated, never created or destroyed. The bank unwinds its locks in reverse order. A privileged admin override lets an operator move a unit directly between any two locations, bypassing the lock stack, but even the override only relocates a unit and never changes the total. The override can be toggled on and off.

The actions are: take the coarse bank lock, take a fine lock on a source location, move a unit from the fine-locked source to a destination, drop the fine lock, drop the coarse lock, admin-move a unit between two locations bypassing the locks, and toggle the admin override.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of blood units across all storage locations is always exactly the amount the bank started with, since every move only relocates a unit and never creates or destroys any.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m4p2t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Tickets

VARIABLES yard, ship, loading, pend
\* yard/ship: containers resting in the yard and on the ship; loading:
\* containers currently in a crane's grip mid-move; pend: outstanding move
\* tickets in the bounded work queue, processed in any order.

vars == <<yard, ship, loading, pend>>

Total == 3
QCap == 2

TypeOK ==
    /\ yard \in 0..Total
    /\ ship \in 0..Total
    /\ loading \in 0..Total
    /\ pend \subseteq Tickets

Init ==
    /\ yard = Total
    /\ ship = 0
    /\ loading = 0
    /\ pend = {}

\* Enqueue a move ticket; backpressure blocks this when the queue is full.
Enqueue(t) ==
    /\ t \notin pend
    /\ Cardinality(pend) < QCap
    /\ pend' = pend \cup {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yard, ship, loading>>

\* A ticket is consumed in any order; a crane lifts a container from the yard.
PickYard(t) ==
    /\ t \in pend
    /\ yard > 0
    /\ yard' = yard - 1
    /\ loading' = loading + 1
    /\ pend' = pend \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED ship

\* Or a crane lifts a container from the ship.
PickShip(t) ==
    /\ t \in pend
    /\ ship > 0
    /\ ship' = ship - 1
    /\ loading' = loading + 1
    /\ pend' = pend \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED yard

\* A held container is set down in the yard.
DropYard ==
    /\ loading > 0
    /\ loading' = loading - 1
    /\ yard' = yard + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ship, pend>>

\* A held container is set down on the ship.
DropShip ==
    /\ loading > 0
    /\ loading' = loading - 1
    /\ ship' = ship + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yard, pend>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Tickets : Enqueue(t)
    \/ \E t \in Tickets : PickYard(t)
    \/ \E t \in Tickets : PickShip(t)
    \/ DropYard
    \/ DropShip

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every lift and set-down only relocates one container among the yard, the
\* ship, and a crane's grip, so the grand total is invariant -- even though
\* move tickets are processed out of order.
Conserved == yard + ship + loading = Total
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Tickets = {q1, q2, q3}
INVARIANT Conserved
nl:
A container-ship crane yard moves containers between the yard and the ship using cranes, driven by a bounded work queue of move tickets with backpressure. Tickets are enqueued, but when the queue is full, backpressure blocks further enqueues. Because tickets flow over a dispatch layer that can reorder messages, they are processed in any order. Processing a ticket makes a crane lift one container -- from either the yard or the ship -- into its grip; a held container is later set down, either in the yard or on the ship. Every lift and every set-down only relocates a single container among the yard, the ship, and a crane's grip; no container is ever created or destroyed.

The actions are: enqueue a move ticket unless backpressure blocks it, consume a ticket to lift a container from the yard into a grip, consume a ticket to lift a container from the ship into a grip, set a held container down in the yard, and set a held container down on the ship.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of containers -- those in the yard, those on the ship, and those held mid-move in a crane's grip -- is always exactly the starting total, since every move only relocates one container and never creates or destroys any.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m9p6t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Stations, Authorized

VARIABLES epoch, inbox, setBy, setEpoch
\* epoch: current reconfiguration epoch; inbox: in-flight command messages, each
\* stamped with the emitting station and epoch (delivered in any order); setBy:
\* station that last set the conveyor; setEpoch: epoch of that setting.

vars == <<epoch, inbox, setBy, setEpoch>>

None == "none"
MaxE == 1
Msgs == [st : Stations, ep : 0..MaxE]

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxE
    /\ inbox \subseteq Msgs
    /\ setBy \in Stations \cup {None}
    /\ setEpoch \in 0..MaxE

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ setBy = None
    /\ setEpoch = 0

\* Any station may emit a command, stamped with the current epoch.
Emit(s) ==
    /\ [st |-> s, ep |-> epoch] \notin inbox
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[st |-> s, ep |-> epoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, setBy, setEpoch>>

\* A command takes effect only if it is fresh (current epoch) and from an
\* authorized station; it is applied in any delivery order.
Apply(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ m.ep = epoch
    /\ m.st \in Authorized
    /\ setBy' = m.st
    /\ setEpoch' = epoch
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

\* A stale command (an old epoch, e.g. left over across a reconfiguration) is
\* rejected.
DropStale(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ m.ep # epoch
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, setBy, setEpoch>>

\* A fresh command from an unauthorized station is rejected.
DropUnauth(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ m.ep = epoch
    /\ m.st \notin Authorized
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, setBy, setEpoch>>

\* A reconfiguration opens a new epoch and clears the current setting, so any
\* command still in flight from the old epoch becomes stale.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxE
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ setBy' = None
    /\ setEpoch' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED inbox

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Stations : Emit(s)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Apply(m)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : DropStale(m)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : DropUnauth(m)
    \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Whenever the conveyor carries a setting, it was made by an authorized station
\* acting at the live epoch, so no unauthorized or stale participant ever takes
\* effect.
NoBadAction ==
    (setBy # None) => (setBy \in Authorized /\ setEpoch = epoch)
=============================================================================
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line is driven by control stations that send commands to set the conveyor, coordinated by epoch-numbered reconfiguration. Any station may emit a command, and each command is stamped with the station's identity and the epoch current when it was emitted. Commands travel over a bus that can reorder messages, so they are delivered and processed in any order. A command takes effect only if it is fresh -- carrying the current epoch -- and comes from an authorized station; when it takes effect, it records itself as the station that set the conveyor at the current epoch. A stale command, carrying an epoch left over from before a reconfiguration, is rejected, and a fresh command from an unauthorized station is also rejected. A reconfiguration opens a new epoch and clears the current setting, which makes any command still in flight from the old epoch stale.

The actions are: a station emits a command stamped with the current epoch, a fresh authorized command is applied in any order (setting the conveyor), a stale command is rejected, a fresh unauthorized command is rejected, and a reconfiguration opens a new epoch and clears the setting.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the conveyor carries a setting, it was made by an authorized station acting at the live epoch, so no unauthorized or stale participant ever takes effect.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m7p2t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers

VARIABLES free, allocated, ver, op, snap, override
\* free/allocated: runway slots free vs allocated (they sum to the fixed total);
\* ver: the compare-and-swap version register; op: the update each controller is
\* attempting; snap: version it read; override: admin override engaged.

vars == <<free, allocated, ver, op, snap, override>>

Total == 2
MaxV == 2
None == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ free \in 0..Total
    /\ allocated \in 0..Total
    /\ ver \in 0..MaxV
    /\ op \in [Controllers -> {None, "alloc", "release"}]
    /\ snap \in [Controllers -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ override \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ free = Total
    /\ allocated = 0
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ op = [c \in Controllers |-> None]
    /\ snap = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
    /\ override = FALSE

\* A controller reads the version and stages an allocate or release.
Read(c, o) ==
    /\ op[c] = None
    /\ o \in {"alloc", "release"}
    /\ op' = [op EXCEPT ![c] = o]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, allocated, ver, override>>

\* Compare-and-swap an allocation: only if the version is unchanged.
CommitAlloc(c) ==
    /\ op[c] = "alloc"
    /\ snap[c] = ver
    /\ ver < MaxV
    /\ free > 0
    /\ free' = free - 1
    /\ allocated' = allocated + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ op' = [op EXCEPT ![c] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, override>>

\* Compare-and-swap a release: only if the version is unchanged.
CommitRelease(c) ==
    /\ op[c] = "release"
    /\ snap[c] = ver
    /\ ver < MaxV
    /\ allocated > 0
    /\ allocated' = allocated - 1
    /\ free' = free + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ op' = [op EXCEPT ![c] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, override>>

\* A stale compare-and-swap (version moved) is dropped.
Fail(c) ==
    /\ op[c] # None
    /\ snap[c] # ver
    /\ op' = [op EXCEPT ![c] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, allocated, ver, snap, override>>

\* Under admin override, allocate a slot directly.
AdminAlloc ==
    /\ override
    /\ ver < MaxV
    /\ free > 0
    /\ free' = free - 1
    /\ allocated' = allocated + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<op, snap, override>>

\* Under admin override, release a slot directly.
AdminRelease ==
    /\ override
    /\ ver < MaxV
    /\ allocated > 0
    /\ allocated' = allocated - 1
    /\ free' = free + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<op, snap, override>>

\* When the version register saturates it is compacted, clearing attempts.
Compact ==
    /\ ver = MaxV
    /\ ver' = 0
    /\ op' = [c \in Controllers |-> None]
    /\ snap' = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, allocated, override>>

\* Toggle the admin override.
ToggleOverride ==
    /\ override' = ~override
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, allocated, ver, op, snap>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, o \in {"alloc", "release"} : Read(c, o)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : CommitAlloc(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : CommitRelease(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Fail(c)
    \/ AdminAlloc
    \/ AdminRelease
    \/ Compact
    \/ ToggleOverride

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every allocate or release only moves a slot between free and allocated, so
\* the total number of runway slots is invariant.
Conserved == free + allocated = Total
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2}
INVARIANT Conserved
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator tracks a fixed set of runway slots, each either free or allocated, coordinated through a compare-and-swap version register. A controller reads the current version and stages either an allocate or a release. It then commits by compare-and-swap: the update takes effect only if the version has not moved since the read, and committing advances the version. An allocate moves one slot from free to allocated; a release moves one slot from allocated back to free -- slots are only ever moved, never created or destroyed. If the version has moved, the compare-and-swap is stale and is dropped. A privileged admin override lets an operator allocate or release a slot directly, still only moving a slot between the two pools. When the version register saturates it is compacted back to zero, clearing any staged attempts. The override can be toggled on and off.

The actions are: read the version and stage an allocate or release, commit an allocate by compare-and-swap, commit a release by compare-and-swap, drop a stale attempt, admin-allocate directly, admin-release directly, compact the saturated version register, and toggle the admin override.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of free runway slots plus the number of allocated slots always equals the fixed total, since every allocate or release only moves a slot between free and allocated.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m5p6t5 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Approvers, Authorized, Requesters

VARIABLES round, appr, holder, grantRound, byAdmin, override
\* round: current approval round; appr: the round each approver last approved
\* (0=none); holder: requester granted the spool; grantRound: round of the
\* grant; byAdmin: grant came via admin override; override: override engaged.

vars == <<round, appr, holder, grantRound, byAdmin, override>>

None == "none"
MaxR == 2
Quorum == 2
CurrentAuthApprovers == {a \in Authorized : appr[a] = round}

TypeOK ==
    /\ round \in 0..MaxR
    /\ appr \in [Approvers -> 0..MaxR]
    /\ holder \in Requesters \cup {None}
    /\ grantRound \in 0..MaxR
    /\ byAdmin \in BOOLEAN
    /\ override \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ round = 0
    /\ appr = [a \in Approvers |-> 0]
    /\ holder = None
    /\ grantRound = 0
    /\ byAdmin = FALSE
    /\ override = FALSE

\* Only an authorized approver may approve, and only for the current round.
Approve(a) ==
    /\ a \in Authorized
    /\ appr[a] # round
    /\ appr' = [appr EXCEPT ![a] = round]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, holder, grantRound, byAdmin, override>>

\* Grant the spool to a requester when a quorum of authorized approvers have
\* approved this very round.
Grant(r) ==
    /\ holder = None
    /\ Cardinality(CurrentAuthApprovers) >= Quorum
    /\ holder' = r
    /\ grantRound' = round
    /\ byAdmin' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, appr, override>>

\* A new round supersedes all prior approvals and any standing grant.
NewRound ==
    /\ round < MaxR
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ appr' = [a \in Approvers |-> 0]
    /\ holder' = None
    /\ grantRound' = 0
    /\ byAdmin' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED override

\* The privileged admin override grants the spool directly, bypassing quorum.
AdminGrant(r) ==
    /\ override
    /\ holder = None
    /\ holder' = r
    /\ grantRound' = round
    /\ byAdmin' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, appr, override>>

\* The holder releases the spool.
Release ==
    /\ holder # None
    /\ holder' = None
    /\ grantRound' = 0
    /\ byAdmin' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, appr, override>>

\* Toggle the admin override.
ToggleOverride ==
    /\ override' = ~override
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, appr, holder, grantRound, byAdmin>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Approvers : Approve(a)
    \/ \E r \in Requesters : Grant(r)
    \/ NewRound
    \/ \E r \in Requesters : AdminGrant(r)
    \/ Release
    \/ ToggleOverride

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Whenever the spool is held, either it was taken via the admin override, or it
\* was granted this round backed by a quorum of authorized approvers -- so no
\* unauthorized or stale participant ever obtains the spool on its own.
NoBadAction ==
    (holder # None) =>
        (byAdmin \/ (grantRound = round /\ Cardinality(CurrentAuthApprovers) >= Quorum))
=============================================================================
nl:
A print shop job spooler grants exclusive use of the spool to one requester at a time, and each grant must be authorized by quorum voting among the approvers. Approvals are organized into rounds. Only an authorized approver may approve, and only for the current round; an approval carrying an old round no longer counts. The spool is granted to a requester when a quorum of authorized approvers have approved the current round, and the grant records the round it was made in. A new round supersedes all prior approvals and any standing grant, so stale approvals and stale grants are swept away. A privileged admin override lets an operator grant the spool directly, bypassing the quorum; such a grant is marked as taken via the override. The holder later releases the spool. The override can be toggled on and off.

The actions are: an authorized approver approves the current round, grant the spool to a requester on a current-round quorum, open a new round (clearing approvals and any grant), the admin grants the spool directly bypassing quorum, the holder releases the spool, and toggle the admin override.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the spool is held, either it was taken via the admin override or it was granted in the current round backed by a quorum of authorized approvers, so no unauthorized or stale participant ever obtains the spool on its own.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od19m2p4t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Replicas, Shelves

VARIABLES reserved, phase, target, votes
\* reserved: reservations held per shelf; phase: idle/voting; target: the shelf
\* a reservation is being voted on; votes: each replica catalog's 2PC ballot.

vars == <<reserved, phase, target, votes>>

Cap == 2
AllYes == \A r \in Replicas : votes[r] = "yes"
SomeNo == \E r \in Replicas : votes[r] = "no"

TypeOK ==
    /\ reserved \in [Shelves -> 0..Cap]
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting"}
    /\ target \in Shelves
    /\ votes \in [Replicas -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]

Init ==
    /\ reserved = [s \in Shelves |-> 0]
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ target \in Shelves
    /\ votes = [r \in Replicas |-> "none"]

\* Open a two-phase commit to reserve a copy on a shelf.
Propose(s) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ target' = s
    /\ votes' = [r \in Replicas |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED reserved

\* A replica catalog prepares (agrees to the reservation).
VoteYes(r) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ votes[r] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![r] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, phase, target>>

\* A replica refuses.
VoteNo(r) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ votes[r] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![r] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, phase, target>>

\* Commit only when unanimous AND the shelf still has room.
Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ AllYes
    /\ reserved[target] < Cap
    /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![target] = reserved[target] + 1]
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<target, votes>>

\* Abort on a refusal, on a full shelf, or on timeout waiting for a slow replica.
Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, target, votes>>

\* A held reservation is later cancelled, freeing shelf space.
Cancel(s) ==
    /\ reserved[s] > 0
    /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![s] = reserved[s] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, target, votes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Shelves : Propose(s)
    \/ \E r \in Replicas : VoteYes(r)
    \/ \E r \in Replicas : VoteNo(r)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ \E s \in Shelves : Cancel(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No shelf ever holds more reservations than its fixed capacity.
BoundedCapacity == \A s \in Shelves : reserved[s] <= Cap
=============================================================================
nl:
A library book reservation system holds reservations on shelves, each with a fixed capacity that must never be exceeded, and commits every new reservation with a two-phase commit across the replica catalogs. The coordinator opens a vote to reserve a copy on a shelf; each replica catalog prepares (agrees) or refuses. Replicas may be slow but never fail, so a round may abort simply because the coordinator times out waiting for a slow replica to vote. A reservation commits only when every replica has prepared and the target shelf still has room; if any replica refuses, the shelf is already full, or the coordinator times out, the round aborts and nothing is reserved. A held reservation is later cancelled, which frees shelf space.

The actions are: open a two-phase commit to reserve on a shelf, a replica prepares, a replica refuses, commit a unanimous round when the shelf has room, abort a round (on refusal, a full shelf, or a slow-replica timeout), and cancel a held reservation.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No shelf ever holds more reservations than its fixed capacity.

spec_text:
--------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m8p0t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Machines

VARIABLES coarse, fine, inCS, want
\* coarse: machine holding the network-wide coarse lock (or none); fine: machine
\* holding the fine vault lock (or none); inCS: machines using the shared vault;
\* want: machines that have signalled intent to access the vault.

vars == <<coarse, fine, inCS, want>>

None == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in Machines \cup {None}
    /\ fine \in Machines \cup {None}
    /\ inCS \in [Machines -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ want \in [Machines -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ coarse = None
    /\ fine = None
    /\ inCS = [m \in Machines |-> FALSE]
    /\ want = [m \in Machines |-> FALSE]

\* A machine signals intent to reach the shared vault.
Request(m) ==
    /\ ~want[m]
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, inCS>>

\* Take the coarse network-wide lock first.
LockCoarse(m) ==
    /\ want[m]
    /\ coarse = None
    /\ coarse' = m
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, inCS, want>>

\* Then take the fine vault lock.
LockFine(m) ==
    /\ coarse = m
    /\ fine = None
    /\ fine' = m
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, inCS, want>>

\* Only the fine-lock holder may use the vault.
Enter(m) ==
    /\ fine = m
    /\ ~inCS[m]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, want>>

\* Leave the vault.
Exit(m) ==
    /\ inCS[m]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, want>>

\* Drop the fine lock once outside the vault.
UnlockFine(m) ==
    /\ fine = m
    /\ ~inCS[m]
    /\ fine' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, inCS, want>>

\* Drop the coarse lock and clear the intent.
UnlockCoarse(m) ==
    /\ coarse = m
    /\ fine = None
    /\ coarse' = None
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, inCS>>

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Request(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : LockCoarse(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : LockFine(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Enter(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Exit(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : UnlockFine(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : UnlockCoarse(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Anyone using the vault holds the fine vault lock; since that lock has a
\* single holder, at most one machine ever uses the vault at a time.
MutualExclusion == \A m \in Machines : inCS[m] => fine = m

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Machines = {m1, m2, m3}
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A vending machine network shares a single cash vault that only one machine may use at a time. Access is arranged with hierarchical locks: a machine first signals intent, then takes a coarse network-wide lock, and only then takes the fine vault lock; it must hold the coarse lock to acquire the fine one. Only the fine-lock holder may use the vault as its critical section, and it leaves the vault when done. Machines may be slow but never fail, so any machine may take arbitrarily long between steps, yet locks are always eventually released rather than held forever by a crashed machine. A machine unwinds in reverse: drop the fine vault lock once outside the vault, then drop the coarse lock and clear its intent. Because the fine vault lock has a single holder, the two machines can never both be using the vault at once.

The actions are: signal intent, take the coarse network lock, take the fine vault lock while holding the coarse lock, enter the vault as the fine-lock holder, leave the vault, drop the fine lock when outside, and drop the coarse lock and clear intent.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any machine using the vault holds the fine vault lock, and since that lock has a single holder, at most one machine ever uses the vault at a time.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od14m0p0t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Drones

VARIABLES owner, ver, reading, snap, inCS
\* owner: drone holding the shared comms channel (or none); ver: version of the
\* lock state; reading: drones that optimistically observed the channel free;
\* snap: the version each observed; inCS: drones using the channel.

vars == <<owner, ver, reading, snap, inCS>>

None == "none"
MaxV == 2

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in Drones \cup {None}
    /\ ver \in 0..MaxV
    /\ reading \in [Drones -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ snap \in [Drones -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ inCS \in [Drones -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ owner = None
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ reading = [d \in Drones |-> FALSE]
    /\ snap = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ inCS = [d \in Drones |-> FALSE]

\* Optimistically observe the channel as free, remembering the version.
Read(d) ==
    /\ ~reading[d]
    /\ owner = None
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![d] = TRUE]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![d] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, inCS>>

\* Commit the acquire only if still free at the observed version (no conflict).
Acquire(d) ==
    /\ reading[d]
    /\ owner = None
    /\ ver = snap[d]
    /\ ver < MaxV
    /\ owner' = d
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![d] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, inCS>>

\* A conflict (channel taken, or the version moved) forces a retry.
Retry(d) ==
    /\ reading[d]
    /\ (owner # None \/ ver # snap[d])
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![d] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, snap, inCS>>

\* Only the owner may use the channel.
Enter(d) ==
    /\ owner = d
    /\ ~inCS[d]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![d] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, reading, snap>>

\* Leave the channel.
Exit(d) ==
    /\ inCS[d]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![d] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, reading, snap>>

\* Release the channel once outside it.
Release(d) ==
    /\ owner = d
    /\ ~inCS[d]
    /\ owner' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, reading, snap, inCS>>

\* When the version saturates and the channel is free, compact it.
Compact ==
    /\ owner = None
    /\ ver = MaxV
    /\ ver' = 0
    /\ reading' = [d \in Drones |-> FALSE]
    /\ snap' = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, inCS>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Read(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Acquire(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Retry(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Enter(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Exit(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Release(d)
    \/ Compact

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Anyone using the channel is its current owner; since there is a single
\* owner, at most one drone ever uses the channel at a time.
MutualExclusion == \A d \in Drones : inCS[d] => owner = d
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Drones = {a1, a2}
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm shares a single directional comms channel that only one drone may use at a time, and access is arranged with optimistic locking with retry. A drone optimistically observes the channel as free and remembers the version it saw. It then tries to commit the acquire: the acquire succeeds only if the channel is still free and its version is unchanged since the read, meaning no other drone slipped in; committing advances the version. If the channel has been taken or the version has moved -- even through a full acquire-and-release cycle -- the observation is in conflict and the drone must retry from scratch. Drones may be slow but never fail, so a drone may take arbitrarily long between steps, yet the channel is always eventually released. Only the owner may use the channel, and it releases the channel once done. When the version saturates and the channel is free, it is compacted back to zero.

The actions are: optimistically observe the channel free (recording the version), commit the acquire when still free at that version, retry on a conflict, the owner enters the channel, the owner leaves the channel, the owner releases the channel, and compact a saturated version.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any drone using the channel is its current owner, and since there is a single owner at a time, at most one drone ever uses the channel at once.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m9p0t5 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Machines

VARIABLES token, holder, heldToken, inCS, override
\* token: current fencing/epoch number; holder: machine holding the current
\* lease (or none); heldToken: fencing token each machine was issued; inCS:
\* machines using the shared assay bench; override: admin override engaged.

vars == <<token, holder, heldToken, inCS, override>>

None == "none"
MaxT == 2

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in 0..MaxT
    /\ holder \in Machines \cup {None}
    /\ heldToken \in [Machines -> 0..MaxT]
    /\ inCS \in [Machines -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ override \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ holder = None
    /\ heldToken = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ inCS = [m \in Machines |-> FALSE]
    /\ override = FALSE

\* Granting a free lease opens a new epoch and issues its fencing token.
Grant(m) ==
    /\ holder = None
    /\ token < MaxT
    /\ token' = token + 1
    /\ holder' = m
    /\ heldToken' = [heldToken EXCEPT ![m] = token + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inCS, override>>

\* Only the machine bearing the current fencing token may use the bench.
Enter(m) ==
    /\ holder = m
    /\ heldToken[m] = token
    /\ ~inCS[m]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, holder, heldToken, override>>

\* Leave the bench.
Exit(m) ==
    /\ inCS[m]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, holder, heldToken, override>>

\* A reconfiguration revokes the lease, opening a new epoch and fencing the old
\* holder out of the bench in the same step.
Revoke ==
    /\ holder # None
    /\ token < MaxT
    /\ token' = token + 1
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![holder] = FALSE]
    /\ holder' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<heldToken, override>>

\* The admin override force-grants a lease, opening a new epoch and clearing the
\* bench so no stale holder remains.
AdminGrant(m) ==
    /\ override
    /\ token < MaxT
    /\ token' = token + 1
    /\ holder' = m
    /\ heldToken' = [heldToken EXCEPT ![m] = token + 1]
    /\ inCS' = [k \in Machines |-> FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED override

\* When the fencing counter saturates and the bench is free, it is compacted.
Compact ==
    /\ holder = None
    /\ token = MaxT
    /\ token' = 0
    /\ heldToken' = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ inCS' = [m \in Machines |-> FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, override>>

\* Toggle the admin override.
ToggleOverride ==
    /\ override' = ~override
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, holder, heldToken, inCS>>

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Grant(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Enter(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Exit(m)
    \/ Revoke
    \/ \E m \in Machines : AdminGrant(m)
    \/ Compact
    \/ ToggleOverride

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Anyone using the bench bears the current fencing token; since only one
\* machine can bear it, at most one machine ever uses the bench at a time.
MutualExclusion == \A m \in Machines : inCS[m] => heldToken[m] = token
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Machines = {m1, m2, m3}
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker gives one machine at a time exclusive use of a shared assay bench, coordinated by epoch-numbered reconfiguration with fencing tokens. Granting a free lease opens a new epoch and issues the holder a fencing token equal to the new epoch number. Only the machine bearing the current fencing token may use the bench, and it leaves the bench when done. A reconfiguration revokes the current lease: it opens a new epoch and, in the same step, fences the old holder out of the bench, so a stale holder can never keep using the bench once its epoch has passed. A privileged admin override lets an operator force-grant a lease, opening a new epoch and clearing the bench so no stale holder remains. When the fencing counter saturates and the bench is free, it is compacted back to zero. The override can be toggled on and off.

The actions are: grant a free lease with a fresh fencing token, the current-token holder enters the bench, a machine leaves the bench, revoke the lease (fencing the old holder out), the admin force-grants a lease (clearing the bench), compact a saturated counter, and toggle the admin override.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any machine using the bench bears the current fencing token, and since only one machine can bear the current token, at most one machine ever uses the bench at a time.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m9p4t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Schedulers, Rooms

VARIABLES booked, epoch, alive, reqs
\* booked: surgeries booked into each room; epoch: current scheduling epoch;
\* alive: scheduler nodes that have not crashed; reqs: pending booking requests,
\* each stamped with the epoch it was raised in.

vars == <<booked, epoch, alive, reqs>>

Cap == 2
MaxE == 1
Reqs == [room : Rooms, ep : 0..MaxE]

TypeOK ==
    /\ booked \in [Rooms -> 0..Cap]
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxE
    /\ alive \in [Schedulers -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ reqs \subseteq Reqs

Init ==
    /\ booked = [r \in Rooms |-> 0]
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ alive = [s \in Schedulers |-> TRUE]
    /\ reqs = {}

\* A live scheduler proposes a booking, stamped with the current epoch.
Propose(s, r) ==
    /\ alive[s]
    /\ [room |-> r, ep |-> epoch] \notin reqs
    /\ reqs' = reqs \cup {[room |-> r, ep |-> epoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, epoch, alive>>

\* Admit a fresh request only if the room is still below capacity.
Admit(q) ==
    /\ q \in reqs
    /\ q.ep = epoch
    /\ booked[q.room] < Cap
    /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![q.room] = booked[q.room] + 1]
    /\ reqs' = reqs \ {q}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, alive>>

\* A stale request (from a prior epoch) is discarded.
DropStale(q) ==
    /\ q \in reqs
    /\ q.ep # epoch
    /\ reqs' = reqs \ {q}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, epoch, alive>>

\* A fresh request for a full room is rejected.
DropFull(q) ==
    /\ q \in reqs
    /\ q.ep = epoch
    /\ booked[q.room] = Cap
    /\ reqs' = reqs \ {q}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, epoch, alive>>

\* A booked surgery is discharged, freeing capacity.
Discharge(r) ==
    /\ booked[r] > 0
    /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![r] = booked[r] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, alive, reqs>>

\* A reconfiguration opens a new scheduling epoch; old requests go stale.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxE
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, alive, reqs>>

\* At most one scheduler node may crash silently.
Crash(s) ==
    /\ alive[s]
    /\ \A t \in Schedulers : alive[t]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, epoch, reqs>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Schedulers, r \in Rooms : Propose(s, r)
    \/ \E q \in reqs : Admit(q)
    \/ \E q \in reqs : DropStale(q)
    \/ \E q \in reqs : DropFull(q)
    \/ \E r \in Rooms : Discharge(r)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E s \in Schedulers : Crash(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No operating room is ever booked beyond its capacity.
BoundedCapacity == \A r \in Rooms : booked[r] <= Cap
=============================================================================
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler books surgeries into operating rooms, each with a fixed capacity that must never be exceeded, and organizes scheduling into numbered epochs. A live scheduler node proposes a booking, and each proposal is stamped with the epoch it was raised in. A proposal is admitted only if it is fresh -- carrying the current epoch -- and the target room is still below its capacity; a stale proposal from a prior epoch is discarded, and a fresh proposal for a full room is rejected. Booked surgeries are later discharged, freeing capacity. A reconfiguration opens a new scheduling epoch, after which proposals from the old epoch are stale. Any single scheduler node may crash silently and stop participating, but at most one node is lost.

The actions are: a live scheduler proposes an epoch-stamped booking, admit a fresh proposal when the room is below capacity, discard a stale proposal, reject a fresh proposal for a full room, discharge a booked surgery, open a new scheduling epoch, and crash at most one scheduler node.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No operating room is ever booked beyond its fixed capacity.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m6p1t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Writers

VARIABLES ver, record, lease, seen, alive
\* ver: number of committed writes to the shared roster; record: last writer;
\* lease: writer holding the exclusive write lease (or none); seen: version each
\* writer has synced to; alive: writers that have not crashed.

vars == <<ver, record, lease, seen, alive>>

None == "none"
Init0 == "init"
MaxV == 2

TypeOK ==
    /\ ver \in 0..MaxV
    /\ record \in Writers \cup {Init0}
    /\ lease \in Writers \cup {None}
    /\ seen \in [Writers -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ alive \in [Writers -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ record = Init0
    /\ lease = None
    /\ seen = [w \in Writers |-> 0]
    /\ alive = [w \in Writers |-> TRUE]

\* A live writer takes the exclusive write lease.
Acquire(w) ==
    /\ lease = None
    /\ alive[w]
    /\ lease' = w
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, record, seen, alive>>

\* A writer catches up to the current version before it may write.
Sync(w) ==
    /\ alive[w]
    /\ seen[w] < ver
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![w] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, record, lease, alive>>

\* The lease-holder writes only when fully caught up, so it cannot clobber an
\* update it never saw; the write advances the version and stamps the writer.
Write(w) ==
    /\ lease = w
    /\ alive[w]
    /\ seen[w] = ver
    /\ ver < MaxV
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ record' = w
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![w] = ver + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, alive>>

\* Release the write lease.
Release(w) ==
    /\ lease = w
    /\ lease' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, record, seen, alive>>

\* At most one writer may crash silently; a crash frees any lease it held.
Crash(w) ==
    /\ alive[w]
    /\ \A x \in Writers : alive[x]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![w] = FALSE]
    /\ lease' = IF lease = w THEN None ELSE lease
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, record, seen>>

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Writers : Acquire(w)
    \/ \E w \in Writers : Sync(w)
    \/ \E w \in Writers : Write(w)
    \/ \E w \in Writers : Release(w)
    \/ \E w \in Writers : Crash(w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The writer who produced the current version had synced to at least that
\* version, so every committed write built on the latest state -- no update lost.
NoLostUpdate == (ver > 0) => seen[record] >= ver
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Writers = {w1, w2}
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A university course-registration system maintains a shared roster record that several writers update, serialized with lease-based ownership. A live writer takes the exclusive write lease, and only the lease-holder may write. Before writing, a writer must sync -- catch up to the current committed version -- and the lease-holder may write only when it is fully caught up, so it can never clobber an update it never saw. A write advances the version and stamps the writer as the record's author. A writer releases the lease when done. Any single writer may crash silently and stop participating; at most one writer is lost, and a crash frees any lease the crashed writer held so the system does not stall.

The actions are: a live writer takes the write lease, a writer syncs to the current version, the caught-up lease-holder writes (advancing the version and stamping itself), a writer releases the lease, and at most one writer crashes silently (freeing its lease).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The writer who produced the current version had synced to at least that version, so every committed write built on the latest state and no update is ever lost.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m2p3t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Students, Slots, Participants

VARIABLES owner, holds, phase, cs, votes
\* owner: student allocated each slot (or none); holds: slot each student holds
\* (or none); phase: idle/voting; cs: the current claim <<student,slot>>; votes:
\* each participant's 2PC ballot.

vars == <<owner, holds, phase, cs, votes>>

None == "none"
AllYes == \A p \in Participants : votes[p] = "yes"
SomeNo == \E p \in Participants : votes[p] = "no"

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Students \cup {None}]
    /\ holds \in [Students -> Slots \cup {None}]
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting"}
    /\ cs \in [stu : Students, slot : Slots]
    /\ votes \in [Participants -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]

Init ==
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> None]
    /\ holds = [u \in Students |-> None]
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ cs \in [stu : Students, slot : Slots]
    /\ votes = [p \in Participants |-> "none"]

\* A student proposes to claim a free slot (and holds nothing yet).
Propose(u, s) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ owner[s] = None
    /\ holds[u] = None
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ cs' = [stu |-> u, slot |-> s]
    /\ votes' = [p \in Participants |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, holds>>

\* A participant prepares.
VoteYes(p) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ votes[p] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, holds, phase, cs>>

\* A participant refuses.
VoteNo(p) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ votes[p] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, holds, phase, cs>>

\* Commit only if unanimous and the slot is still free and the student free.
Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ AllYes
    /\ owner[cs.slot] = None
    /\ holds[cs.stu] = None
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![cs.slot] = cs.stu]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![cs.stu] = cs.slot]
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cs, votes>>

\* Abort on refusal, on a slot/student that became taken, or on a slow timeout.
Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, holds, cs, votes>>

\* A student releases its slot.
Release(u) ==
    /\ holds[u] # None
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![holds[u]] = None]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![u] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, cs, votes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E u \in Students, s \in Slots : Propose(u, s)
    \/ \E p \in Participants : VoteYes(p)
    \/ \E p \in Participants : VoteNo(p)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ \E u \in Students : Release(u)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every slot a student holds is owned by that same student; since a slot has a
\* single owner, no slot is ever allocated to two students at once.
NoDoubleAllocation == \A u \in Students : holds[u] # None => owner[holds[u]] = u
=============================================================================
nl:
A university course-registration system allocates seat slots to students, and every allocation is committed with a two-phase commit across the participating services so that no slot is ever allocated to two students. A student proposes to claim a free slot while holding none itself; the participants prepare or refuse. Participants may be slow but never fail, so a round may abort because the coordinator times out waiting for a slow participant. A claim commits only if the vote is unanimous and, at commit time, the slot is still free and the student still holds nothing; committing records the student as the slot's owner and the slot as the student's holding, in one step. Otherwise the round aborts. A student later releases its slot, freeing both the owner and the holding.

The actions are: propose a claim on a free slot, a participant prepares, a participant refuses, commit a unanimous claim when the slot and student are still free, abort a round (on refusal, a taken slot, or a slow-participant timeout), and release a held slot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every slot a student holds is owned by that same student, and since a slot has a single owner, no slot is ever allocated to two students at once.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m6p2t1 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Traders, Accounts

VARIABLES bal, lease, ttl, inbox
\* bal: share balance per account; lease: trader holding the ledger lease (or
\* none); ttl: remaining lease ticks; inbox: pending transfer tickets, applied
\* in any order.

vars == <<bal, lease, ttl, inbox>>

None == "none"
Total == 2
MaxTTL == 1
Tickets == {m \in [from : Accounts, to : Accounts] : m.from # m.to}

RECURSIVE SumBal(_)
SumBal(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET a == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN bal[a] + SumBal(S \ {a})

TypeOK ==
    /\ bal \in [Accounts -> 0..Total]
    /\ lease \in Traders \cup {None}
    /\ ttl \in 0..MaxTTL
    /\ inbox \subseteq Tickets

Init ==
    /\ bal = [a \in Accounts |-> IF a = "book" THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ lease = None
    /\ ttl = 0
    /\ inbox = {}

\* A trader takes the ledger lease with a fresh term.
Acquire(t) ==
    /\ lease = None
    /\ lease' = t
    /\ ttl' = MaxTTL
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bal, inbox>>

\* The lease term decays.
Decay ==
    /\ lease # None
    /\ ttl > 0
    /\ ttl' = ttl - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bal, lease, inbox>>

\* An expired lease is released.
Expire ==
    /\ lease # None
    /\ ttl = 0
    /\ lease' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bal, ttl, inbox>>

\* The lease-holder submits a transfer ticket while its term is valid.
Submit(t, m) ==
    /\ lease = t
    /\ ttl > 0
    /\ m \notin inbox
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bal, lease, ttl>>

\* Transfer tickets are applied in any order; each moves one share.
Apply(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ bal[m.from] > 0
    /\ bal' = [bal EXCEPT ![m.from] = @ - 1, ![m.to] = @ + 1]
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, ttl>>

\* A ticket whose source is empty cannot be fulfilled and is dropped.
DropEmpty(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ bal[m.from] = 0
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bal, lease, ttl>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Acquire(t)
    \/ Decay
    \/ Expire
    \/ \E t \in Traders, m \in Tickets : Submit(t, m)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Apply(m)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : DropEmpty(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every applied transfer only moves one share between accounts, so the total
\* number of shares is invariant -- even though tickets are applied out of order.
Conserved == SumBal(Accounts) = Total
=============================================================================
nl:
A stock exchange opening auction settles share transfers among accounts -- the order book, a bidder, and a seller -- through a shared ledger guarded by lease-based ownership with expiry. A trader takes the ledger lease with a fresh term, which decays tick by tick; an expired lease is released. Only the lease-holder, while its term is valid, may submit a transfer ticket naming a source and destination account. Tickets travel over a matching bus that can reorder messages, so they are applied in any order. Applying a ticket moves exactly one share from the source account to the destination; a ticket whose source account is empty cannot be fulfilled and is dropped. Shares are only ever moved between accounts, never created or destroyed.

The actions are: a trader takes the ledger lease with a fresh term, the lease term decays, an expired lease is released, the lease-holder submits a transfer ticket while its term is valid, apply a ticket in any order (moving one share), and drop an unfulfillable ticket.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of shares across all accounts is always exactly the starting total, since every transfer only moves one share between accounts and never creates or destroys any.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m8p5t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Containers, Bays, CapLevels

VARIABLES sealed, sealedBy, level, fineBay, cap
\* sealed: containers irreversibly loaded onto the ship; sealedBy: the bay each
\* sealed container went to (none if unsealed); level: yard lock level; fineBay:
\* the fine-locked bay; cap: per-bay capacity, retuned at runtime.

vars == <<sealed, sealedBy, level, fineBay, cap>>

None == "none"
Load(b) == Cardinality({c \in Containers : sealedBy[c] = b})

TypeOK ==
    /\ sealed \subseteq Containers
    /\ sealedBy \in [Containers -> Bays \cup {None}]
    /\ level \in {"idle", "coarse", "fine"}
    /\ fineBay \in Bays \cup {None}
    /\ cap \in CapLevels

Init ==
    /\ sealed = {}
    /\ sealedBy = [c \in Containers |-> None]
    /\ level = "idle"
    /\ fineBay = None
    /\ cap \in CapLevels

\* Take the coarse yard lock.
LockCoarse ==
    /\ level = "idle"
    /\ level' = "coarse"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sealed, sealedBy, fineBay, cap>>

\* Take a fine lock on a specific loading bay.
LockFine(b) ==
    /\ level = "coarse"
    /\ fineBay = None
    /\ fineBay' = b
    /\ level' = "fine"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sealed, sealedBy, cap>>

\* Irreversibly seal a container into the fine-locked bay, if it fits; the
\* container joins the sealed set and records its bay in one step.
Seal(c) ==
    /\ level = "fine"
    /\ fineBay # None
    /\ c \notin sealed
    /\ Load(fineBay) < cap
    /\ sealed' = sealed \cup {c}
    /\ sealedBy' = [sealedBy EXCEPT ![c] = fineBay]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<level, fineBay, cap>>

\* Drop the fine lock.
UnlockFine ==
    /\ level = "fine"
    /\ level' = "coarse"
    /\ fineBay' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sealed, sealedBy, cap>>

\* Drop the coarse lock.
UnlockCoarse ==
    /\ level = "coarse"
    /\ level' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sealed, sealedBy, fineBay, cap>>

\* Retune the per-bay capacity at runtime, never below any bay's current load.
Recap ==
    /\ \E k \in CapLevels :
        /\ \A b \in Bays : k >= Load(b)
        /\ cap' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sealed, sealedBy, level, fineBay>>

Next ==
    \/ LockCoarse
    \/ \E b \in Bays : LockFine(b)
    \/ \E c \in Containers : Seal(c)
    \/ UnlockFine
    \/ UnlockCoarse
    \/ Recap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A container is in the sealed set exactly when it has a recorded loading bay;
\* since a sealed container is never sealed again, its irreversible load happens
\* at most once.
SealedOnce == \A c \in Containers : (c \in sealed) <=> (sealedBy[c] # None)
=============================================================================
nl:
A container-ship crane yard loads containers into the ship's loading bays, and sealing a container into a bay is irreversible -- once sealed it is committed to the voyage -- so each container is sealed at most once. Sealing is serialized with hierarchical locks: the yard takes a coarse yard-wide lock, then a fine lock on a specific loading bay, before it may seal a container into that bay. A container is sealed only if it has not been sealed before and the fine-locked bay still has room; sealing adds the container to the sealed set and records which bay it went to, in one step. Each bay has a capacity that is retuned at runtime as trim and stability allow, but a bay's capacity is never lowered below the number of containers already sealed into it. The yard unwinds its locks in reverse order.

The actions are: take the coarse yard lock, take a fine lock on a bay, irreversibly seal a container into the fine-locked bay when it fits, drop the fine lock, drop the coarse lock, and retune per-bay capacity at runtime to any level not below any bay's current load.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A container is in the sealed set exactly when it has a recorded loading bay, and since a sealed container is never sealed again, its irreversible load happens at most once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m7p5t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Instances, Items

VARIABLES ver, done, doneBy, attempt, snap
\* ver: per-item compare-and-swap version; done: items irreversibly finalized;
\* doneBy: instance that finalized each item; attempt: item each instance is
\* finalizing; snap: version it observed.

vars == <<ver, done, doneBy, attempt, snap>>

None == "none"
MaxV == 1

TypeOK ==
    /\ ver \in [Items -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ done \subseteq Items
    /\ doneBy \in [Items -> Instances \cup {None}]
    /\ attempt \in [Instances -> Items \cup {None}]
    /\ snap \in [Instances -> 0..MaxV]

Init ==
    /\ ver = [t \in Items |-> 0]
    /\ done = {}
    /\ doneBy = [t \in Items |-> None]
    /\ attempt = [i \in Instances |-> None]
    /\ snap = [i \in Instances |-> 0]

\* An instance reads an unfinalized item's version, staging a finalize.
Read(i, t) ==
    /\ attempt[i] = None
    /\ t \notin done
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![i] = t]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![i] = ver[t]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, done, doneBy>>

\* Finalize by compare-and-swap: only if the item's version is unchanged. The
\* finalize is irreversible; it records the finalizer and bumps the version.
Finalize(i) ==
    /\ attempt[i] # None
    /\ LET t == attempt[i] IN
        /\ t \notin done
        /\ ver[t] = snap[i]
        /\ ver[t] < MaxV
        /\ done' = done \cup {t}
        /\ doneBy' = [doneBy EXCEPT ![t] = i]
        /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![t] = ver[t] + 1]
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![i] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

\* A stale compare-and-swap (version moved) is dropped.
Fail(i) ==
    /\ attempt[i] # None
    /\ ver[attempt[i]] # snap[i]
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![i] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, done, doneBy, snap>>

\* A finalized item is recycled for the next settlement batch.
Recycle(t) ==
    /\ t \in done
    /\ done' = done \ {t}
    /\ doneBy' = [doneBy EXCEPT ![t] = None]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![t] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<attempt, snap>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances, t \in Items : Read(i, t)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Finalize(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Fail(i)
    \/ \E t \in Items : Recycle(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* An item is in the finalized set exactly when it has a recorded finalizer;
\* since a finalized item is never finalized again before recycling, its
\* irreversible settlement happens at most once.
FinalizedOnce == \A t \in Items : (t \in done) <=> (doneBy[t] # None)
=============================================================================
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch runs on two independent processor instances that share one pool of settlement items. Finalizing a settlement is irreversible -- once finalized it is posted -- so each item must be finalized at most once. The two instances coordinate through a per-item compare-and-swap version. An instance reads an unfinalized item's version and stages a finalize. It commits by compare-and-swap: the finalize succeeds only if the item's version is unchanged since the read; committing is irreversible, records which instance finalized the item, and bumps the item's version. If the version has moved -- because the other instance finalized it first -- the compare-and-swap is stale and is dropped. A finalized item is later recycled for the next settlement batch, which clears its finalizer and resets its version.

The actions are: read an unfinalized item's version and stage a finalize, commit the finalize by compare-and-swap (irreversibly, recording the finalizer), drop a stale attempt, and recycle a finalized item.

SAFETY PROPERTY: An item is in the finalized set exactly when it has a recorded finalizer, and since a finalized item is never finalized again before recycling, its irreversible settlement happens at most once.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od16m0p1t1 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Dispensers

VARIABLES ver, reading, snap, inbox, lastSnap
\* ver: version of the shared prescription record; reading: dispensers mid read-
\* modify-write; snap: version each observed; inbox: in-flight commit messages
\* (delivered in any order); lastSnap: version the last applied commit built on.

vars == <<ver, reading, snap, inbox, lastSnap>>

MaxV == 2
Msgs == [disp : Dispensers, base : 0..MaxV]

TypeOK ==
    /\ ver \in 0..MaxV
    /\ reading \in [Dispensers -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ snap \in [Dispensers -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ inbox \subseteq Msgs
    /\ lastSnap \in 0..MaxV

Init ==
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ reading = [d \in Dispensers |-> FALSE]
    /\ snap = [d \in Dispensers |-> 0]
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ lastSnap = 0

\* Optimistically read the current version to modify the record.
Read(d) ==
    /\ ~reading[d]
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![d] = TRUE]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![d] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, inbox, lastSnap>>

\* Submit a commit stamped with the version observed; it joins the reorderable
\* message set.
Submit(d) ==
    /\ reading[d]
    /\ [disp |-> d, base |-> snap[d]] \notin inbox
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[disp |-> d, base |-> snap[d]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, reading, snap, lastSnap>>

\* Apply a commit (in any order) only if its base still matches the current
\* version -- no update slipped in since the read -- advancing the version.
Apply(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ m.base = ver
    /\ ver < MaxV
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ lastSnap' = m.base
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![m.disp] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

\* A stale commit (its base no longer matches) is rejected; the writer retries.
Reject(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ m.base # ver
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![m.disp] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, snap, lastSnap>>

\* When the version saturates the record is compacted.
Compact ==
    /\ ver = MaxV
    /\ ver' = 0
    /\ reading' = [d \in Dispensers |-> FALSE]
    /\ snap' = [d \in Dispensers |-> 0]
    /\ inbox' = {}
    /\ lastSnap' = 0

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers : Read(d)
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers : Submit(d)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Apply(m)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Reject(m)
    \/ Compact

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The last applied commit built on the version immediately below the current
\* one, so every committed update was based on the latest state and no update
\* is ever lost -- even though commits are delivered out of order.
NoLostUpdate == ver > 0 => lastSnap = ver - 1
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Dispensers = {d1, d2}
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser network updates a shared prescription record using optimistic locking with retry. A dispenser optimistically reads the record's current version to begin a modification, remembering the version it saw. It then submits a commit stamped with that observed version. Because commits travel over a network that can reorder messages, they are delivered and applied in any order. A commit is applied only if its stamped base still matches the current version -- meaning no other update slipped in since the read -- and applying advances the version and records the base it built on. If the base no longer matches, the commit is stale and is rejected, so the dispenser must retry from a fresh read. When the version saturates, the record is compacted back to zero.

The actions are: optimistically read the current version, submit a commit stamped with the observed version, apply a commit in any order when its base still matches, reject a stale commit (forcing a retry), and compact a saturated version.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The last applied commit built on the version immediately below the current one, so every committed update was based on the latest state and no update is ever lost, even when commits are delivered out of order.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m1p3t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Runways

VARIABLES token, owner, holds, want
\* token: ring position holding the allocation token; owner: flight allocated
\* each runway (or none); holds: runway each flight holds (or none); want:
\* flights that have requested a runway.

vars == <<token, owner, holds, want>>

NumFlights == 3
Flights == 0..(NumFlights - 1)
None == "none"
NoOwner == NumFlights

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Flights
    /\ owner \in [Runways -> Flights \cup {NoOwner}]
    /\ holds \in [Flights -> Runways \cup {None}]
    /\ want \in [Flights -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ owner = [r \in Runways |-> NoOwner]
    /\ holds = [f \in Flights |-> None]
    /\ want = [f \in Flights |-> FALSE]

\* A flight requests a runway.
Request(f) ==
    /\ ~want[f]
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![f] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, owner, holds>>

\* Only the token-holding flight may allocate, and only a free runway to itself
\* while it holds nothing.
Allocate(f, r) ==
    /\ token = f
    /\ want[f]
    /\ owner[r] = NoOwner
    /\ holds[f] = None
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![r] = f]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![f] = r]
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![f] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED token

\* A flight releases its runway.
Release(f) ==
    /\ holds[f] # None
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![holds[f]] = NoOwner]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![f] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, want>>

\* The token circulates around the ring; a slow flight simply misses its turn.
PassToken ==
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % NumFlights
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, holds, want>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Flights : Request(f)
    \/ \E f \in Flights, r \in Runways : Allocate(f, r)
    \/ \E f \in Flights : Release(f)
    \/ PassToken

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every runway a flight holds is owned by that same flight; since a runway has
\* a single owner, no runway is ever allocated to two flights at once.
NoDoubleAllocation == \A f \in Flights : holds[f] # None => owner[holds[f]] = f
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Runways = {rw1, rw2}
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator grants runways to flights using a token ring for exclusive access. A single allocation token circulates around a ring of flights, and only the flight currently holding the token may allocate a runway. A flight first requests a runway; when it holds the token, it may allocate a free runway to itself, provided it holds no runway already. Allocating records the flight as the runway's owner and the runway as the flight's holding, in one step. Flights may be slow but never fail, so a slow flight simply misses its turn as the token passes, and the token keeps circulating. A flight releases its runway when done, freeing both the owner and the holding.

The actions are: a flight requests a runway, the token-holding flight allocates a free runway to itself, a flight releases its runway, and the token circulates to the next flight around the ring.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every runway a flight holds is owned by that same flight, and since a runway has a single owner, no runway is ever allocated to two flights at once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m4p1t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Updates, CapLevels

VARIABLES submitted, pending, applied, qcap
\* submitted: updates accepted into the system; pending: updates waiting in the
\* bounded work queue; applied: updates written to the shared record; qcap:
\* queue capacity (backpressure), retuned at runtime.

vars == <<submitted, pending, applied, qcap>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ submitted \subseteq Updates
    /\ pending \subseteq Updates
    /\ applied \subseteq Updates
    /\ qcap \in CapLevels

Init ==
    /\ submitted = {}
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ applied = {}
    /\ qcap \in CapLevels

\* Submit an update; backpressure blocks this when the queue is at capacity.
Submit(u) ==
    /\ u \notin submitted
    /\ Cardinality(pending) < qcap
    /\ submitted' = submitted \cup {u}
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {u}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<applied, qcap>>

\* Process a queued update: it moves from the queue to the record atomically.
Process(u) ==
    /\ u \in pending
    /\ pending' = pending \ {u}
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {u}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<submitted, qcap>>

\* A fully applied update is acknowledged and its slot recycled.
Clear(u) ==
    /\ u \in applied
    /\ submitted' = submitted \ {u}
    /\ applied' = applied \ {u}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, qcap>>

\* The queue capacity is retuned at runtime, never below the current backlog.
Recap ==
    /\ \E c \in CapLevels :
        /\ c >= Cardinality(pending)
        /\ qcap' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<submitted, pending, applied>>

Next ==
    \/ \E u \in Updates : Submit(u)
    \/ \E u \in Updates : Process(u)
    \/ \E u \in Updates : Clear(u)
    \/ Recap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every submitted update is always accounted for -- either still queued or
\* already applied to the record -- so no update is ever silently lost.
NoLostUpdate == \A u \in Updates : u \in submitted => (u \in pending \/ u \in applied)
=============================================================================
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator applies configuration updates to a shared record through a bounded work queue with backpressure. An update is submitted into the queue, but when the queue is at its capacity, backpressure blocks further submissions. The queue's capacity is retuned at runtime, never below the current backlog. Processing a queued update moves it from the queue to the shared record atomically, so an update is never dropped between being dequeued and being written. A fully applied update is later acknowledged, recycling its slot. Every submitted update is therefore always accounted for -- either still waiting in the queue or already applied to the record.

The actions are: submit an update unless backpressure blocks it, process a queued update (moving it from the queue to the record), acknowledge and recycle a fully applied update, and retune the queue capacity at runtime to any level not below the current backlog.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every submitted update is always accounted for -- either still queued or already applied to the record -- so no update is ever silently lost.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m5p0t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Voters, CapLevels

VARIABLES owner, inCS, phase, votes, claimant, cap
\* owner: controller holding the wash control arm (or none); inCS: controllers
\* driving the arm; phase: idle/voting; votes: each voter's ballot; claimant:
\* controller a grant is for; cap: current quorum threshold, retuned at runtime.

vars == <<owner, inCS, phase, votes, claimant, cap>>

None == "none"
YesCount == Cardinality({v \in Voters : votes[v] = "yes"})

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in Controllers \cup {None}
    /\ inCS \in [Controllers -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting"}
    /\ votes \in [Voters -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
    /\ claimant \in Controllers \cup {None}
    /\ cap \in CapLevels

Init ==
    /\ owner = None
    /\ inCS = [c \in Controllers |-> FALSE]
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ votes = [v \in Voters |-> "none"]
    /\ claimant = None
    /\ cap \in CapLevels

\* A controller opens a vote to be granted the control arm.
Request(c) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ owner = None
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ claimant' = c
    /\ votes' = [v \in Voters |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, inCS, cap>>

\* A voter approves.
VoteYes(v) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ votes[v] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![v] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, inCS, phase, claimant, cap>>

\* A voter objects.
VoteNo(v) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ votes[v] = "none"
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![v] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, inCS, phase, claimant, cap>>

\* Grant only when approvals meet the current quorum threshold.
Grant ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ YesCount >= cap
    /\ owner = None
    /\ owner' = claimant
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ claimant' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inCS, votes, cap>>

\* The vote fails to reach quorum and is abandoned.
Deny ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ claimant' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, inCS, votes, cap>>

\* Only the owner may drive the control arm.
Enter(c) ==
    /\ owner = c
    /\ ~inCS[c]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, phase, votes, claimant, cap>>

\* Leave the critical section.
Exit(c) ==
    /\ inCS[c]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, phase, votes, claimant, cap>>

\* Release the control arm once outside the section.
Release(c) ==
    /\ owner = c
    /\ ~inCS[c]
    /\ owner' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inCS, phase, votes, claimant, cap>>

\* The quorum threshold is retuned at runtime.
Recap ==
    /\ \E k \in CapLevels : cap' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, inCS, phase, votes, claimant>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Request(c)
    \/ \E v \in Voters : VoteYes(v)
    \/ \E v \in Voters : VoteNo(v)
    \/ Grant
    \/ Deny
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Enter(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Exit(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Release(c)
    \/ Recap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Anyone driving the control arm is its current owner; since there is a single
\* owner, at most one controller ever drives the arm at a time.
MutualExclusion == \A c \in Controllers : inCS[c] => owner = c
=============================================================================
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line has a single control arm that only one controller may drive at a time, and the right to drive it is granted by quorum voting. A controller opens a vote to be granted the arm; each voter approves or objects. The grant succeeds only when the number of approvals meets the current quorum threshold, which is itself a capacity that is retuned at runtime as staffing changes. If the approvals never meet the threshold, the vote is abandoned. Only the granted owner may drive the control arm as its critical section, and it leaves the section when done. The owner releases the arm once it is outside the section. Because the arm has a single owner at any time, no two controllers can ever both be driving it at once.

The actions are: open a grant vote, a voter approves, a voter objects, grant the arm when approvals meet the current quorum threshold, abandon a vote that never reaches quorum, the owner enters the section, a controller leaves the section, the owner releases the arm, and retune the quorum threshold at runtime.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any controller driving the control arm is its current owner, and since there is a single owner at a time, at most one controller ever drives the arm at once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m7p1t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Writers

VARIABLES ver, record, reading, snap, seen
\* ver: version of the shared settlement record; record: last writer; reading:
\* writers mid compare-and-swap; snap: version each observed; seen: version each
\* writer has synced to.

vars == <<ver, record, reading, snap, seen>>

Init0 == "init"
MaxV == 2

TypeOK ==
    /\ ver \in 0..MaxV
    /\ record \in Writers \cup {Init0}
    /\ reading \in [Writers -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ snap \in [Writers -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ seen \in [Writers -> 0..MaxV]

Init ==
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ record = Init0
    /\ reading = [w \in Writers |-> FALSE]
    /\ snap = [w \in Writers |-> 0]
    /\ seen = [w \in Writers |-> 0]

\* A writer reads the current version to begin a compare-and-swap.
Read(w) ==
    /\ ~reading[w]
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![w] = TRUE]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![w] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, record, seen>>

\* Commit by compare-and-swap: only if the version is unchanged since the read,
\* so a lagging writer cannot clobber an update it never saw. The writer becomes
\* current as it commits.
Commit(w) ==
    /\ reading[w]
    /\ snap[w] = ver
    /\ ver < MaxV
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ record' = w
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![w] = ver + 1]
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![w] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

\* A stale compare-and-swap (version moved) is dropped.
Fail(w) ==
    /\ reading[w]
    /\ snap[w] # ver
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![w] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, record, snap, seen>>

\* A lagging writer catches up to the current version.
Sync(w) ==
    /\ seen[w] < ver
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![w] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, record, reading, snap>>

\* When the version saturates the record is compacted.
Compact ==
    /\ ver = MaxV
    /\ ver' = 0
    /\ record' = Init0
    /\ reading' = [w \in Writers |-> FALSE]
    /\ snap' = [w \in Writers |-> 0]
    /\ seen' = [w \in Writers |-> 0]

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Writers : Read(w)
    \/ \E w \in Writers : Commit(w)
    \/ \E w \in Writers : Fail(w)
    \/ \E w \in Writers : Sync(w)
    \/ Compact

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The writer who produced the current version had synced to at least that
\* version, so every committed write built on the latest state and no update is
\* ever lost.
NoLostUpdate == ver > 0 => seen[record] >= ver
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Writers = {w1, w2}
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch updates a shared settlement record using a compare-and-swap version register. A writer reads the current version to begin an update. It commits by compare-and-swap: the write takes effect only if the version has not moved since the read, which means a lagging writer cannot clobber an update it never saw; the writer becomes current as it commits, advancing the version and stamping itself as the record's author. If the version has moved, the compare-and-swap is stale and is dropped, and the writer retries. A lagging writer may independently sync -- catch up to the current version. Writers may be slow but never fail, so a writer may take arbitrarily long between reading and committing, and a slow writer that falls behind is simply forced to retry rather than losing anyone's update. When the version saturates, the record is compacted.

The actions are: read the current version, commit by compare-and-swap when the version is unchanged (advancing the version and stamping the writer), drop a stale attempt, sync a lagging writer to the current version, and compact a saturated version.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The writer who produced the current version had synced to at least that version, so every committed write built on the latest state and no update is ever lost.
