---------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m8p2t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Feeders, CapLevels

VARIABLES active, shed, level, fineFeeder, cap
\* active/shed: load served vs shed per feeder (they sum to the feeder's fixed
\* load); level: grid lock level (idle/coarse/fine); fineFeeder: the fine-locked
\* feeder; cap: max shed per feeder, retuned at runtime.

vars == <<active, shed, level, fineFeeder, cap>>

FTotal == 2
None == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ active \in [Feeders -> 0..FTotal]
    /\ shed \in [Feeders -> 0..FTotal]
    /\ level \in {"idle", "coarse", "fine"}
    /\ fineFeeder \in Feeders \cup {None}
    /\ cap \in CapLevels

Init ==
    /\ active = [f \in Feeders |-> FTotal]
    /\ shed = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
    /\ level = "idle"
    /\ fineFeeder = None
    /\ cap \in CapLevels

\* Take the coarse grid-wide lock.
LockCoarse ==
    /\ level = "idle"
    /\ level' = "coarse"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, shed, fineFeeder, cap>>

\* Take a fine lock on a specific feeder.
LockFine(f) ==
    /\ level = "coarse"
    /\ fineFeeder = None
    /\ fineFeeder' = f
    /\ level' = "fine"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, shed, cap>>

\* Shed one unit of load on the fine-locked feeder, within the shed capacity.
Shed(f) ==
    /\ level = "fine"
    /\ fineFeeder = f
    /\ active[f] > 0
    /\ shed[f] < cap
    /\ active' = [active EXCEPT ![f] = active[f] - 1]
    /\ shed' = [shed EXCEPT ![f] = shed[f] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<level, fineFeeder, cap>>

\* Restore one unit of shed load back to service on the fine-locked feeder.
Restore(f) ==
    /\ level = "fine"
    /\ fineFeeder = f
    /\ shed[f] > 0
    /\ shed' = [shed EXCEPT ![f] = shed[f] - 1]
    /\ active' = [active EXCEPT ![f] = active[f] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<level, fineFeeder, cap>>

\* Drop the fine lock.
UnlockFine ==
    /\ level = "fine"
    /\ level' = "coarse"
    /\ fineFeeder' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, shed, cap>>

\* Drop the coarse lock.
UnlockCoarse ==
    /\ level = "coarse"
    /\ level' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, shed, fineFeeder, cap>>

\* Retune the per-feeder shed capacity at runtime, never below any current shed.
Recap ==
    /\ \E k \in CapLevels :
        /\ \A f \in Feeders : k >= shed[f]
        /\ cap' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, shed, level, fineFeeder>>

Next ==
    \/ LockCoarse
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : LockFine(f)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Shed(f)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Restore(f)
    \/ UnlockFine
    \/ UnlockCoarse
    \/ Recap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Shedding and restoring only move load between served and shed on a feeder, so
\* each feeder's served plus shed load always equals its fixed total.
Conserved == \A f \in Feeders : active[f] + shed[f] = FTotal
=============================================================================
nl:
A power-grid load shedder manages, for each feeder, a fixed amount of load that is at any moment either served or shed. Shedding operations are serialized with hierarchical locks: the operator takes a coarse grid-wide lock, then a fine lock on a specific feeder, before it may shed or restore load on that feeder. Shedding moves one unit of load from served to shed, subject to a per-feeder shed capacity; restoring moves one unit from shed back to served. Load is only ever moved between served and shed on a feeder, never created or destroyed. The per-feeder shed capacity is retuned at runtime as the emergency evolves, but it is never lowered below any feeder's current shed. The operator unwinds its locks in reverse order.

The actions are: take the coarse grid lock, take a fine lock on a feeder, shed one unit on the fine-locked feeder within capacity, restore one unit on the fine-locked feeder, drop the fine lock, drop the coarse lock, and retune the per-feeder shed capacity at runtime to any level not below any feeder's current shed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every feeder, its served load plus its shed load always equals its fixed total, since shedding and restoring only move load between served and shed.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m9p1t5 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Writers

VARIABLES ver, record, epoch, seen, override
\* ver: committed writes to the shared assay record; record: last writer; epoch:
\* reconfiguration epoch; seen: version each writer has synced to; override:
\* admin override engaged.

vars == <<ver, record, epoch, seen, override>>

Init0 == "init"
MaxV == 2
MaxE == 2

TypeOK ==
    /\ ver \in 0..MaxV
    /\ record \in Writers \cup {Init0}
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxE
    /\ seen \in [Writers -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ override \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ record = Init0
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ seen = [w \in Writers |-> 0]
    /\ override = FALSE

\* A lagging writer syncs to the current version.
Sync(w) ==
    /\ seen[w] < ver
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![w] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, record, epoch, override>>

\* A caught-up writer commits, so it cannot clobber an update it never saw.
Write(w) ==
    /\ seen[w] = ver
    /\ ver < MaxV
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ record' = w
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![w] = ver + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, override>>

\* An epoch reconfiguration archives the record and starts a fresh version line.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxE
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ ver' = 0
    /\ record' = Init0
    /\ seen' = [w \in Writers |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED override

\* The admin override force-writes, keeping the writer marked current.
AdminWrite(w) ==
    /\ override
    /\ ver < MaxV
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ record' = w
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![w] = ver + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, override>>

\* When the version saturates within an epoch, the record is compacted.
Compact ==
    /\ ver = MaxV
    /\ ver' = 0
    /\ record' = Init0
    /\ seen' = [w \in Writers |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, override>>

\* Toggle the admin override.
ToggleOverride ==
    /\ override' = ~override
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, record, epoch, seen>>

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Writers : Sync(w)
    \/ \E w \in Writers : Write(w)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E w \in Writers : AdminWrite(w)
    \/ Compact
    \/ ToggleOverride

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The writer who produced the current version had synced to at least that
\* version, so every committed write built on the latest state -- no update lost.
NoLostUpdate == ver > 0 => seen[record] >= ver
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Writers = {w1, w2}
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker keeps a shared assay record updated by several writers, organized into numbered reconfiguration epochs. A lagging writer first syncs -- catches up to the current committed version. Only a caught-up writer may commit a write, so it can never clobber an update it never saw; committing advances the version and stamps the writer as the record's author. An epoch reconfiguration archives the current record and starts a fresh version line at a new epoch. A privileged admin override lets an operator force-write, but the forced write still marks the writer as current, so the record stays consistent. When the version saturates within an epoch, the record is compacted. The override can be toggled on and off.

The actions are: sync a lagging writer to the current version, a caught-up writer commits (advancing the version and stamping itself), reconfigure to a new epoch (archiving the record), the admin force-writes, compact a saturated version, and toggle the admin override.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The writer who produced the current version had synced to at least that version, so every committed write built on the latest state and no update is ever lost.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od17m4p2t1 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Carousels

VARIABLES bags, queue, arm, armDest
\* bags: bag count on each carousel; queue: reorderable routing tickets in the
\* bounded work queue; arm: whether the router arm is carrying a bag (0/1);
\* armDest: the destination remembered for the carried bag.

vars == <<bags, queue, arm, armDest>>

Total == 2
QCap == 2
None == "none"
Tickets == {t \in [from : Carousels, to : Carousels] : t.from # t.to}

RECURSIVE SumBags(_)
SumBags(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET c == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN bags[c] + SumBags(S \ {c})

TypeOK ==
    /\ bags \in [Carousels -> 0..Total]
    /\ queue \subseteq Tickets
    /\ arm \in 0..1
    /\ armDest \in Carousels \cup {None}

Init ==
    /\ bags = [c \in Carousels |-> IF c = "intake" THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ queue = {}
    /\ arm = 0
    /\ armDest = None

\* Enqueue a routing ticket; backpressure blocks this when the queue is full.
Enqueue(t) ==
    /\ t \notin queue
    /\ Cardinality(queue) < QCap
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bags, arm, armDest>>

\* Pick up a bag for a queued ticket (in any order), remembering its destination.
Pick(t) ==
    /\ t \in queue
    /\ arm = 0
    /\ bags[t.from] > 0
    /\ bags' = [bags EXCEPT ![t.from] = bags[t.from] - 1]
    /\ arm' = 1
    /\ armDest' = t.to
    /\ queue' = queue \ {t}

\* Set the carried bag down on its remembered destination carousel.
Place ==
    /\ arm = 1
    /\ bags' = [bags EXCEPT ![armDest] = bags[armDest] + 1]
    /\ arm' = 0
    /\ armDest' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED queue

\* A ticket whose source carousel is empty cannot be served and is dropped.
Drop(t) ==
    /\ t \in queue
    /\ bags[t.from] = 0
    /\ queue' = queue \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bags, arm, armDest>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Tickets : Enqueue(t)
    \/ \E t \in Tickets : Pick(t)
    \/ Place
    \/ \E t \in Tickets : Drop(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every pick-and-place only relocates one bag among the carousels and the arm,
\* so the total bag count is invariant -- even though tickets are served out of
\* order.
Conserved == SumBags(Carousels) + arm = Total
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Carousels = {"intake", "sortA", "sortB"}
INVARIANT Conserved
nl:
An airport baggage router moves bags among carousels -- the intake belt and two sorting carousels -- driven by a bounded work queue of routing tickets with backpressure. A ticket names a source and destination carousel. Tickets are enqueued, but when the queue is full, backpressure blocks further enqueues. Because tickets flow over a sortation controller that can reorder messages, they are served in any order. Serving a ticket makes the router arm pick up one bag from the source carousel, remembering the ticket's destination; the carried bag is later set down on that destination carousel. A ticket whose source carousel is empty cannot be served and is dropped. Every pick-and-place only relocates a single bag among the carousels and the arm; no bag is ever created or destroyed.

The actions are: enqueue a routing ticket unless backpressure blocks it, pick up a bag for a queued ticket in any order (remembering the destination), place the carried bag on its destination carousel, and drop a ticket whose source is empty.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of bags -- those on the carousels plus the one possibly held by the router arm -- is always exactly the starting total, since every move only relocates one bag and never creates or destroys any.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m1p1t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumTraders

VARIABLES ver, record, token, seen
\* ver: committed writes to the shared order book; record: last writer; token:
\* ring position holding the write token; seen: version each trader has synced.

vars == <<ver, record, token, seen>>

Traders == 0..(NumTraders - 1)
Init0 == "init"
MaxV == 2

TypeOK ==
    /\ ver \in 0..MaxV
    /\ record \in Traders \cup {Init0}
    /\ token \in Traders
    /\ seen \in [Traders -> 0..MaxV]

Init ==
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ record = Init0
    /\ token = 0
    /\ seen = [t \in Traders |-> 0]

\* The write token circulates; a slow trader simply misses its turn.
PassToken ==
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % NumTraders
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, record, seen>>

\* A lagging trader syncs to the current version.
Sync(t) ==
    /\ seen[t] < ver
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![t] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, record, token>>

\* Only the token-holder, and only when caught up, may write; it thus cannot
\* clobber an update it never saw.
Write(t) ==
    /\ token = t
    /\ seen[t] = ver
    /\ ver < MaxV
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ record' = t
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![t] = ver + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED token

\* When the version saturates the order book is compacted.
Compact ==
    /\ ver = MaxV
    /\ ver' = 0
    /\ record' = Init0
    /\ seen' = [t \in Traders |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED token

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Sync(t)
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Write(t)
    \/ Compact

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The trader who produced the current version had synced to at least that
\* version, so every committed write built on the latest order book -- no update
\* is ever lost.
NoLostUpdate == ver > 0 => seen[record] >= ver
=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    NumTraders = 3
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A stock exchange opening auction maintains a shared order book that several traders update, serialized by a token ring. A single write token circulates around a ring of traders, and only the trader currently holding the token may write. Before writing, a trader must sync -- catch up to the current committed version -- and the token-holder may write only when it is fully caught up, so it can never clobber an update it never saw. A write advances the version and stamps the trader as the order book's last author. Traders may be slow but never fail, so a slow trader simply misses its turn as the token passes, and the token keeps circulating rather than stalling on a slow node. When the version saturates, the order book is compacted.

The actions are: the write token circulates to the next trader, a lagging trader syncs to the current version, the caught-up token-holder writes (advancing the version and stamping itself), and compact a saturated version.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The trader who produced the current version had synced to at least that version, so every committed write built on the latest order book and no update is ever lost.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m4p6t2 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Participants, Authorized

VARIABLES gen, queue, setBy, setGen
\* gen: current generation of the shared dispenser; queue: bounded work queue of
\* requests, each stamped with requester and generation; setBy: participant that
\* last set the dispenser; setGen: generation of that setting.

vars == <<gen, queue, setBy, setGen>>

None == "none"
MaxG == 1
QCap == 2
Msgs == [who : Participants, g : 0..MaxG]

TypeOK ==
    /\ gen \in 0..MaxG
    /\ queue \subseteq Msgs
    /\ setBy \in Participants \cup {None}
    /\ setGen \in 0..MaxG

Init ==
    /\ gen = 0
    /\ queue = {}
    /\ setBy = None
    /\ setGen = 0

\* Enqueue a request stamped with the current generation; backpressure blocks
\* this when the shared queue is full.
Enqueue(p) ==
    /\ [who |-> p, g |-> gen] \notin queue
    /\ Cardinality(queue) < QCap
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {[who |-> p, g |-> gen]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, setBy, setGen>>

\* A request takes effect only if it is fresh (current generation) and from an
\* authorized participant.
Process(m) ==
    /\ m \in queue
    /\ m.g = gen
    /\ m.who \in Authorized
    /\ setBy' = m.who
    /\ setGen' = gen
    /\ queue' = queue \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED gen

\* A stale request (old generation) is discarded.
DropStale(m) ==
    /\ m \in queue
    /\ m.g # gen
    /\ queue' = queue \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, setBy, setGen>>

\* A fresh request from an unauthorized participant is discarded.
DropUnauth(m) ==
    /\ m \in queue
    /\ m.g = gen
    /\ m.who \notin Authorized
    /\ queue' = queue \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, setBy, setGen>>

\* Bumping the generation invalidates the current setting and all older requests.
Bump ==
    /\ gen < MaxG
    /\ gen' = gen + 1
    /\ setBy' = None
    /\ setGen' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED queue

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Participants : Enqueue(p)
    \/ \E m \in queue : Process(m)
    \/ \E m \in queue : DropStale(m)
    \/ \E m \in queue : DropUnauth(m)
    \/ Bump

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Whenever the dispenser carries a setting, it was made by an authorized
\* participant acting at the current generation, so no unauthorized or stale
\* participant ever takes effect.
NoBadAction == (setBy # None) => (setBy \in Authorized /\ setGen = gen)
=============================================================================
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker runs two independent instances that share one dispenser, fed by a single bounded work queue with backpressure. Requests to set the dispenser are enqueued, each stamped with the requester and the generation current when it was raised; when the shared queue is full, backpressure blocks further enqueues. A request takes effect only if it is fresh -- carrying the current generation -- and comes from an authorized participant, namely one of the two sharing instances; taking effect records that instance as having set the dispenser at the current generation. A stale request from an older generation is discarded, and a fresh request from an unauthorized outside participant is also discarded. Bumping the generation invalidates the current setting and makes every older request stale. Both instances draw from and feed the one shared queue.

The actions are: enqueue a generation-stamped request unless backpressure blocks it, process a fresh authorized request (setting the dispenser), discard a stale request, discard a fresh unauthorized request, and bump the generation (invalidating the setting and older requests).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the dispenser carries a setting, it was made by an authorized instance acting at the current generation, so no unauthorized or stale participant ever takes effect.
